title: When the Protocol Burns Again
premise: Paloma Joubert, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Vesper's Cradle, intercepts a distress call in a dead language and realizes the station has been broadcasting a forged ceasefire protocol between two rival fleets for a decade—a lie inherited from the predecessor who vanished. As both fleets converge on the relay to claim or destroy it, Paloma must decide whether to preserve the deception that keeps two million people from war or expose the truth that could shatter it. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the real signal alongside the forgery, forcing both fleets to confront the lie together, and chooses to stay aboard as the living witness to an honest peace.
about_author: Ada Iversen is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years listening to frequencies no one else answered before turning to fiction. She writes about lonely outposts, inherited secrets, and the voices we keep alive long after they should have gone silent.

chapters.title: The Frequency That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Paloma, alone on the Vesper's Cradle for ten years, detects a distress signal in a language extinct since the Meridian Collapse. While tracing its origin through the station's archives, they stumble into a sealed sublevel containing their predecessor's logs—and evidence that the station's celebrated ceasefire broadcast is a fabrication. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet unease curdling into betrayal as home becomes a crime scene.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Liars
chapters.summary: Reading the vanished technician Osei's final entries, Paloma learns the forged protocol was built from a genuine treaty that failed—patched with hope and held together by daily maintenance neither fleet knows is human. A patrol drone arrives asking questions Paloma can't safely answer, and they perform normalcy while deciding whether to keep feeding the lie. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: reluctant guardianship; grief for Osei becoming loyalty to his impossible choice.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Signal
chapters.summary: Both fleets arrive in contested orbit, each believing the other broke the protocol when a solar storm corrupts the forged broadcast. Paloma races to repair the signal while hails turn hostile and weapons arm; in the chaos they discover the distress call was Osei's own, sent years ago, still looping—a plea for someone to end the deception. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: terror under fire transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Protocol Was For
chapters.summary: Paloma broadcasts everything—the original failed treaty, the forgery, Osei's confession—to both fleets at once, gambling that shared truth beats managed peace. Commanders on both sides hesitate, then open direct talks brokered by the station itself. Paloma declines evacuation, staying as the relay's human voice. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: catharsis and chosen solitude; identity found not in hiding but in witness.
